codeReview.summary: The content_generator skill is fully and correctly implemented at commit aa872d8, covering all 4 required actions (blog_post, social_copy, email_copy, brand_voice). All 45 tests pass. The implementation follows codebase conventions (BaseSkill pattern, list-style manifest parameters, async DB operations). CRITICAL PROCESS NOTE: The handoff from worker session cfc580d4 (commitId 1646957) actually implemented market_intelligence, not content_generator. The content_generator was implemented in a separate commit (aa872d8) by a different process. Despite the session tracking mismatch, the feature requirements are fully met in the codebase.

issues.description: Empty __init__.py file added — most other skills (social_media, market_intelligence, email_marketing, etc.) do not have __init__.py files. Minor inconsistency with codebase patterns, but not harmful.

_load_brand_voice() creates a new AsyncSessionLocal for each call. This is fine for correctness but could be optimized by accepting an optional session parameter for reuse when brand_voice is loaded during content generation actions (blog_post, social_copy, email_copy all call it).
social_copy prompt uses chr(10) for newline in f-string (chr(10).join(platform_specs)). While functional, this is a less readable pattern — could use a pre-joined variable instead.

_parse_blog_sections: The section detection heuristic is fragile — it relies on LLM output matching exact patterns like '## Introduction', '## Conclusion'. If LLM uses different headers (e.g., '### Introduction' or '**Introduction**'), parsing may put content in wrong sections. The fallback (lines 316-319) handles complete parse failure, but partial mismatch could produce odd section splits.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Worker session cfc580d4 was assigned feature 'skill-content-generation' but implemented 'market_intelligence' instead (commit 1646957). The handoff salientSummary, whatWasImplemented, commit message, and all verification commands reference market_intelligence. The actual content_generator was implemented in a separate commit (aa872d8). This indicates a feature-assignment/routing confusion in the orchestration layer — the same worker session appears in both skill-content-generation.completedWorkerSessionId AND skill-market-intelligence.workerSessionIds.

The content_generator skill includes an empty __init__.py, while most other skills (social_media, market_intelligence, email_marketing, calendar, backup_automation) do not. AGENTS.md and architecture.md do not specify whether __init__.py should be present in skill directories.

summary: PASS with process observations. The content_generator skill is well-implemented with all 4 required actions (blog_post, social_copy, email_copy, brand_voice), comprehensive tests (45 passing), brand voice integration via system_knowledge, and proper error handling. The code follows established patterns (BaseSkill, list-style manifest, async DB). However, the worker session (cfc580d4) that is tracked as completing this feature actually implemented market_intelligence (commit 1646957) — the content_generator code lives at commit aa872d8 from a different process. No blocking code issues found; 4 non-blocking observations noted (unnecessary __init__.py, repeated session creation, chr(10) readability, fragile section parsing).
